title: Zariski degree-zero comparison for a proper scheme over a henselian pair
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $Z=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ [def-pc-fibre-product], viewed as a closed subset of the underlying topological space of $X$ (the projection $Z\to X$ is a closed immersion, the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$). For every sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on the underlying topological space of $X$, the restriction map $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal F|_Z)$ is bijective, where $\mathcal F|_Z$ is the topological inverse image of $\mathcal F$ along the inclusion $i:Z\subseteq X$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image], taken with values in sets: the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] $\theta:i_p\mathcal F\to\mathcal F|_Z$ of the presheaf $i_p\mathcal F:U\mapsto\varinjlim_{V\supseteq U}\mathcal F(V)$ ($V$ open in $X$; colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] with coprojections $\iota^U_V$), and the restriction map is $s\mapsto\theta_Z(\iota^Z_X(s))$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.91.1, Tag 0A0B (label lemma-zariski-h0-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 18167); its proof uses Tag 09ZG (lemma-h0-topological), Tag 094L, Tag 03H2 (Stein factorization, general), Tag 09XK (integral over henselian pair), Tag 09Y6 (irreducible henselian pair connected), Tag 0377

proof.text: *Step 1 (the closed fibre over $V(I)$; $X$ is spectral).* Let $g:W\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be any morphism of schemes and $W_0=W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ with first projection $p:W_0\to W$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion], so is $p$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], i.e. $p$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset $p(W_0)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The image of $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $V(I)$ (the primes of $A/I$ are the $\mathfrak q/I$ with $\mathfrak q\supseteq I$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]). By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points], $w\in W$ lies in $p(W_0)$ iff there are $s_0\in\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ with image $s=g(w)$ and a prime of $\kappa(w)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s_0)$; such a prime always exists, since a tensor product of two nonzero vector spaces over the field $\kappa(s)$ is a nonzero ring. Hence $p(W_0)=g^{-1}(V(I))$. For $W=X$, $g=f$: the closed subset of the statement is $Z=f^{-1}(V(I))$. Moreover $f$ is proper, hence separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], and its underlying space is spectral [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral].

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 59.91.1 (Tag 0A0B, line 18167): 'the underlying topological space of $X$ is spectral by Properties, Lemma 094L'; the identification of $Y\cap Z$ with $Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$

proof.text: *Step 2 (reduction to a connectedness statement).* By Step 1, $X$ is spectral and $Z\subseteq X$ is closed. By [lem-weil-pbc-h0-spectral-closed-restriction] (applied to the sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$, with $\mathcal F|_Z$ and the restriction map as in the statement, which are those of [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] with values in sets), $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal F|_Z)$ is bijective as soon as $Z\cap\overline{\{x\}}$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] (in particular nonempty) for every $x\in X$. Steps 3 to 6 prove this for a fixed $x\in X$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 59.91.1 (Tag 0A0B, line 18167): 'We will use Lemma 09ZG to prove this'

proof.text: *Step 3 (replacing $X$ by an irreducible closed subscheme).* Let $T=\overline{\{x\}}$; it is closed and irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] (if $T=C_1\cup C_2$ with $C_i$ closed then $x\in C_i$ for some $i$, so $T\subseteq C_i$). By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme] there is a closed immersion $j:Y\to X$ with $j(Y)=T$; $j$ is a homeomorphism of $Y$ onto $T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], so $Y$ is irreducible. A closed immersion is proper and a composite of proper morphisms is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (c), (a), so $g=f\circ j:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is proper. Put $Y_0=g^{-1}(V(I))=j^{-1}(f^{-1}(V(I)))=j^{-1}(Z)$ (Step 1); $Y_0$ is closed in $Y$, and by Step 1 applied to $W=Y$ it is the image of $Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to Y$. Since $j$ is a homeomorphism onto $T$, it maps $Y_0$ homeomorphically onto $T\cap Z$. So it suffices to show that $Y_0$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme].

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 59.91.1 (Tag 0A0B, line 18167): 'Let $Y\subset X$ be an irreducible closed subscheme. ... we show that $Y\cap Z=Y\times_{\Spec(A)}\Spec(A/I)$ is connected. Replacing $X$ by $Y$ we may assume that $X$ is irreducible'

proof.text: *Step 4 (Stein factorization).* Let $Y\xrightarrow{q}\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{s}\operatorname{Spec}A$ be the Stein factorization of the proper $g$ [def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization], $B=H^0(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$, $\varphi:A\to B$ the structure map, $g=s\circ q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-stein-factorization-affine], $A\to B$ is integral, $q$ is proper, and for every $t\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ the subspace $q^{-1}(t)\subseteq Y$ is connected (in particular nonempty). By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-over-henselian-pair], $(B,IB)$ is a henselian pair.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 59.91.1 (Tag 0A0B, line 18167): 'Let $X\to\Spec(B)\to\Spec(A)$ be the Stein factorization of $f$ (Theorem 03H2). Then $A\to B$ is integral and $(B,IB)$ is a henselian pair (Lemma 09XK). Thus we may assume the fibres of $X\to\Spec(A)$ are geometrically connected'

proof.text: *Step 5 (the image of $Y$ meets $V(IB)$ in a connected set).* Let $T'=q(Y)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$. It is closed, since $q$ is proper, hence universally closed, hence (base change along the identity) a closed map [def-weil-proper-morphism]; and it is irreducible, as the image of the irreducible $Y$ under a continuous map (if $T'=C_1\cup C_2$ with $C_i$ closed, then $Y=q^{-1}(C_1)\cup q^{-1}(C_2)$, so $Y=q^{-1}(C_i)$ and $T'\subseteq C_i$ for some $i$) [def-weil-irreducible-components]. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober], $T'$ has a generic point $\mathfrak q$, so $T'=\overline{\{\mathfrak q\}}=V(\mathfrak q)$ (the closure of a point $\mathfrak q$ of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the smallest $V(J)$ containing it, which is $V(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]). Further $s^{-1}(V(I))=V(IB)$: a prime $\mathfrak r\subseteq B$ has $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak r)\supseteq I$ iff $\varphi(I)\subseteq\mathfrak r$ iff $IB\subseteq\mathfrak r$. Hence $T'\cap s^{-1}(V(I))=V(\mathfrak q)\cap V(IB)=V(\mathfrak q+IB)$, which is connected (in particular nonempty) by [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-prime-connected] applied to the henselian pair $(B,IB)$ (Step 4) and the prime $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 59.91.1 (Tag 0A0B, line 18167): 'the image $T\subset\Spec(A)$ of $f$ is irreducible and closed as $X$ is proper over $A$. Hence $T\cap V(I)$ is connected by More on Algebra, Lemma 09Y6' (here with $A$ replaced by $B$)

proof.text: *Step 6 ($Y_0$ is connected).* Put $W=V(\mathfrak q+IB)=T'\cap V(IB)$ (Step 5). By Step 3 and $g=s\circ q$, $Y_0=g^{-1}(V(I))=q^{-1}(s^{-1}(V(I)))=q^{-1}(V(IB))$, so $q$ restricts to a continuous map $h:Y_0\to W$ (subspace topologies), $h(y)=q(y)\in q(Y)\cap V(IB)=W$. It is surjective: for $w\in W\subseteq T'=q(Y)$ pick $y$ with $q(y)=w$; then $y\in q^{-1}(V(IB))=Y_0$. Its fibres $h^{-1}(w)=q^{-1}(w)$ are connected for $w\in W$ (Step 4). It is closed: a closed subset $C$ of $Y_0$ is closed in $Y$ ($Y_0$ is closed in $Y$), so $h(C)=q(C)$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ (Step 5: $q$ is a closed map) and hence in $W$. Therefore $W$ carries the quotient topology for $h$: if $h^{-1}(S)$ is closed for some $S\subseteq W$, then $S=h(h^{-1}(S))$ (surjectivity) is closed; conversely preimages of closed sets are closed by continuity. Since $W$ is connected (Step 5), [lem-weil-pbc-connected-fibres-quotient-preimage-connected] gives that $Y_0=h^{-1}(W)$ is connected. By Step 3, $Z\cap\overline{\{x\}}$ is connected for every $x\in X$, and Step 2 concludes.
